clue.text: Call round with bullish expression?

parts.note: to call, as in ringing for someone, is to bell
a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a bull to hear what it has to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a bull's expression is its roar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull's characteristic loud cry is described with this word for a deep roar.

clue.text: Renewal of lease isn't something that's required

indicators.note: renewal means making again, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Renewing a tenancy agreement is not obligatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential is a necessity, a thing you cannot do without.

clue.text: Crazy motions raised within fringes of Labour Party

indicators.note: within puts the reversed piece inside the edge letters
the fringes of the phrase are its very first and last letters
raised in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: motions in the bowel-movement sense are poo

explanation.surface: Mad proposals put forward at the margins of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motions' are not proposals but bowel movements; 'fringes' gives L and Y of 'Labour Party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is an informal word for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Evidence of underground activity sat around after 24 turned on presenter

indicators.note: on means placed above the next piece in a down entry
after puts the rearranged letters at the end
turned means the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: 24 points to the answer at 24 down; a synonym of it is row, a din
MC, master of ceremonies, is a presenter

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A TV presenter sat around after a din turned on them.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' is not a number but the answer to 24 down, used here through its synonym; 'turned' reverses it and 'around' shuffles 'sat'. 'on' places the reversed word above the presenter in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm leaves a coiled pile of soil at the surface, showing it is burrowing below.

clue.text: Area beneath earth's crust shifting end of continental shelf

indicators.note: shifting tells us one letter of the geological layer is moved to a new spot

parts.note: the geological mantle lies beneath the crust

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A geology lesson about the edge of the continental shelf moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental shelf' reads as a geology term, but 'shelf' alone is the definition; moving L (end of 'continental') to the end of MANTLE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantelpiece is the ledge above a fireplace, a kind of shelf.

clue.text: Recall author's written about city affected by revolution

indicators.note: written about means the setter's possessive is placed around the next part

parts.note: the author is the setter, so author's is my

indicators.note: revolution turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A writer recalls a city changed by a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author's' is the setter's MY; 'revolution' turns ROME into EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory is the faculty of recall, a noun matching recall as a noun.

clue.text: Country divided by a king and queen is telling

indicators.note: divided by means the other letters split the country

parts.note: a country is a nation
R stands for rex, Latin for king
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A nation split by a monarch and consort's rule is revealing.
explanation.walkthrough: R for both king (rex) and queen (regina) is standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the act of recounting a story, the noun sense of telling.

clue.text: Former partner has charge reduced to much acclaim

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: reduced means shortened by a letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge for passage

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's legal charge is reduced to great applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' clips TOLL to TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, and much acclaim as a verb phrase is just that.

clue.text: Sceptic starts to think highly of meaningless arguments, surprisingly

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A doubter who, surprisingly, rates pointless debate highly.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostle Doubting Thomas would not believe in the Resurrection without proof.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubting Thomas is the proverbial sceptic, after the apostle.

clue.text: Capital fellow supporting end to casual working

indicators.note: supporting means placed below the other parts in a down entry
the end of the word is its final letter

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A fellow in a capital city backs an end to casual labour.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is an Oxford or Cambridge college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Recall hurt followed after man's blocked presentation of facts

indicators.note: after places the reversed part behind the possessive word

parts.note: belonging to a man is his

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the following letters are read backwards

parts.note: to mar is to hurt or spoil
followed, as in understood, is got (I got it)

explanation.surface: A man was blocked from giving his presentation, and the pain followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' reverses MARGOT to give TOGRAM. 'blocked' belongs to the definition: the facts are shown as blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: This chart shows data as adjacent bars or blocks, so it is a block-built display of figures.

clue.text: Proportion equal to 5/9 of 6

indicators.note: five ninths of means keeping just five letters of a nine-letter word

parts.note: 6 points to the entry at 6 down, the word clued as telling

explanation.surface: A maths sum: a fraction of six is equal to a ratio.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is not a number but the answer to 6 down; keep five of its nine letters, dropping NAR and the last N.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses one quantity relative to another, which is what a proportion is.

clue.text: Capital united in misery following evacuation

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: united as one

explanation.surface: A capital city's people united in misery after being evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following evacuation' empties 'misery' of its middle letters, and 'Capital' means wealth, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is wealth or funds, a synonym for cash.

clue.text: Cut short rude TV chef making comeback

parts.note: curt means brusque or rude

indicators.note: making a comeback means the name runs backwards

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook

explanation.surface: A rude television chef makes a return to screens.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a long-running British TV cook; 'making comeback' reverses DELIA to AILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to cut it short, so the past form matches.

clue.text: Diagnostic method with fewest resources

definitions.meaning: an allergy check where substances are applied to the skin
skint is British slang for broke, so the most skint has the least money

explanation.surface: A medical procedure chosen because it costs the least.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for penniless; SKINTEST is its jokey superlative, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors test for allergies by applying substances to the skin; and the poorest person is the most broke.

clue.text: Factious Labour organisation split over black university lecturer

parts.note: TU is a trade union, a workers' body

indicators.note: over means covering, so the split surrounds the following letters

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome union split over a black academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it means workers, giving TU.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent people are unruly and quarrelsome, as factious ones are.

clue.text: Independent article leaving American statesman unblemished

indicators.note: leaving says these letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: read as state's man: a man of the US state Virginia
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An independent politician quits an American statesman's party, untainted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' is read as state's man: a man from the US state of Virginia. 'leaving' removes the independent and the article from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin snow or a virgin page is untouched and pure, without a mark.

clue.text: Sort of care given cause for complaint

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so these letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The kind of care received prompted a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is a wrong that someone feels entitles them to protest.

clue.text: Without a coat as it's hot and stuffy

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
a stuffy room lacks fresh air

explanation.surface: Going without a coat since the weather is hot and close.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal with no fur or bald skin lacks a coat, so it is bare-skinned.

clue.text: Draw every flower in Yorkshire

parts.note: every one means all
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch every bloom growing in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river (it flows), not a bloom; the Ure flows through North Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to attract them, the sense of allure as a verb.

clue.text: One aiming to pull strings with striking results

definitions.text: One aiming to pull strings with striking results

parts.words: One aiming to pull strings with striking results
parts.note: a bowman aims, draws back the bowstring and hits the target

explanation.walkthrough: 'pull strings' suggests wielding influence, but here it is literally drawing a bowstring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman draws a string and aims arrows that strike a target.

clue.text: Moan endlessly about relative visiting often

indicators.note: about means surrounding the relative
endlessly means with both end letters dropped

parts.note: to whinge is to moan, chiefly British
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone complains constantly about a relative who drops in all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips WHINGE to HING, which goes about AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost that haunts a place keeps frequenting it, so haunting means repeatedly visiting.

clue.text: Glean audience's perception of African country

indicators.note: what an audience perceives is what it hears, so this is about sound

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Gather how listeners see an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner information is to gather or collect it, as gleaners gather grain.

clue.text: Promote rule of law in training up whistleblower

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the training

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
R is an abbreviation for rule in legal citation

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a referee, or ref, blows the whistle

explanation.surface: Promoting the rule of law by training up a whistleblower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistleblower' suggests an informant but is the referee; 'up' reverses REF to FER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer someone in an older sense is to advance them to a post or rank.

clue.text: Victor's someone who plays with his nuts we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound

parts.words: someone who plays with his nuts
parts.note: conkers is a British children's game played with horse chestnuts on strings

explanation.surface: A cheeky hint about a winner who fiddles with himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British schoolyard game where players swing horse chestnuts on strings to smash an opponent's; a player would be a conkerer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who defeats an enemy in battle is the victor.

clue.text: Talent for discovery disrupted by one's interference

indicators.note: disrupted by means broken into by another piece

parts.note: a nose for news is a talent for discovering things
one is I, the Roman numeral; 's is the possessive

explanation.surface: A gift for discovery thwarted by someone's meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I, the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Interference on a radio or signal is heard as unwanted sound, static.

clue.text: Continually losing men in agitated state

indicators.note: losing means these letters are taken away

parts.note: forever means continually
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A unit endlessly losing soldiers is in a nervous state.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever pitch of excitement is a state of nervous agitation.

clue.text: Topsoil often covers up leaves

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters read upwards
covers means the clue words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Topsoil frequently covers fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' conceals OILOF in 'Topsoil often'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet or leaf of a book, and leaves are pages.

clue.text: Cover in employee's case is cut off

indicators.note: in means the cover sits between the casing letters
a word's case is its outside letters

parts.note: a lid covers a container

explanation.surface: An employee's insurance cover was cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outer letters E and E of 'employee's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide a vowel or syllable is to omit or strike it in speech.

clue.text: Clean using self-employed contractor

parts.note: read the answer's parts as an instruction: set the letters of lance free and they make the word clean

explanation.surface: A cleaner who is a self-employed contractor.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as anagram indicator plus fodder, would produce 'Clean'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer sells their services to clients without being on a payroll.

clue.text: Put off by entering on the right-hand side

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other piece

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
X means by, as in measurements such as two by four

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from entering a building on its right side.
explanation.walkthrough: X stands for 'by' as in dimensions (3 x 4).
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic term for the right side of a shield.

clue.text: One feeding flames of coup bringing resistance to an end

indicators.note: bringing a letter somewhere signals it is moved
to an end says where the moved letter goes: the last position

parts.note: a stroke of luck or a masterstroke is a coup
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A political firebrand fuels the flames of a coup until resistance is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving R in STROKE to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker shovels fuel into a furnace, as on steam engines and ships.
